findings.text: the four-line axis.set_title call (fontsize=6) prints the 12-value shared level array as one unwrapped line roughly 140 characters wide, and matplotlib's default title placement neither wraps nor clips it to the axes width; in the rendered translated-40mm.png (opened with the image tool) the 'levels Wb (shared): [...]' line is truncated at the figure's left margin on every row ('ls Wb (shared)' instead of 'levels Wb (shared)') and overruns into the neighbouring panel's own title on the right ('43.4,49.69Wb (shared): [-19.51...' where the two panels' text collides), on all three rows of the 2x3 poloidal grid. The receipt's titles array (which the test suite reads) carries the correct, complete strings, so tests/test_fixture_positional_stiffness_render.py passes while a human reader of the PNG cannot read the level array or, in row 1, the word 'levels' itself. This is a rendering-layout defect the receipt-driven gate is structurally unable to see.

confirmed by opening both residual PNGs side by side: the 110- and 300-cell figures are visually indistinguishable at print size (identical curve shapes, identical legend, differing only in the title's cell counts), which the landing record discloses honestly rather than hiding ('the pair are merely indistinguishable at print size, their arrays differing by under three percent at 40 mm'). Not a defect in this node's repair — the receipt and pixel digests prove the two are distinct measurements — but the original audit's visual complaint ('pixel-identical: every marker, every curve') is not fully resolved from a reader's standpoint, only from an instrument's; flagged for whoever owns the next rendering pass on this directory, per the node's own follow_ons.

justifications.durability: tests/test_fixture_positional_stiffness_render.py carries no slow marker, so it is collected by the default lane; 5 checks cover the residual-pair distinctness, the on-disk digest match, the printed residual/converged/level-array strings, both null sets on all 6 panels, and an in-lane negative control (test_the_guard_rejects_two_figures_with_one_pixel_digest) that duplicates a pixel digest via monkeypatch and asserts the specific refusal reason — reproduced independently in this review (5 passed, 16.06s) plus a separate out-of-lane reproduction via the NOVA_POSITIONAL_STIFFNESS_IDENTICAL_FIGURES env var matching render-test-negative-control.log verbatim. Docked because every check is receipt/string-driven and none asserts anything about rendered layout, so the title-overflow defect found in this review (see findings) has no regression test and could recur silently.
justifications.evidence: independently reran tests/test_fixture_positional_stiffness_render.py in the target worktree (5 passed, matches manifest) and reran the negative control both ways (in-lane monkeypatch test, and the standalone env-var reproduction), getting the identical AssertionError and colliding digests recorded in render-test-negative-control.log. Opened all four regenerated PNGs with the image tool: the two residual figures are pixel-distinguishable only by their titles and underlying curves are near-identical at print size (as the landing record discloses); translated-40mm.png shows unfilled contour lines on shared levels for both analytic and translated fields, the wall, and both axis markers on all six panels (no X-points, matching null_glyphs x_points_drawn=0 for a fixture where both topologies are limited) — but the level-array title line is genuinely illegible on-image due to a layout overflow the receipt-driven test cannot detect, which is exactly the class of defect the image-tool charge in this review's done-when exists to catch.
justifications.fit: reuses nova.media.poloidal (draw_flux_contours, draw_wall, draw_nulls) and DEFAULT_INK.variant for per-set colour overrides rather than inventing new painters; the receipt/digest scaffolding (pixel_sha256, source_receipt_sha256) is a reasonable minimal addition for the discrimination question the followups asked. Docked for the title construction itself: a 4-line, ~140-character-wide title at fontsize 6 packed into a narrow two-column poloidal grid with no wrapping or width check was foreseeably going to overflow, and did.
justifications.goal_fidelity: both driving followups are answered with a measured, not asserted, verdict: the residual pair are shown to be two distinct measurements (disjoint row selections, distinct file and pixel digests, one shared source receipt) rather than a duplicate render, and every comparison panel now prints residual=/converged=/the shared level array per the render receipt. The convergence flag reading 'no' everywhere at 40 mm is correctly diagnosed as a property of the amplitude relative to the axis-projection scale, not a render defect, and disclosed as a follow-on rather than hidden. Docked because the level-array line the second followup specifically required is present in the receipt's title strings but not reliably legible in the rendered PNG a reader would actually look at (see findings), which is a partial rather than a full resolution of 'states its level array' when judged against the image rather than the JSON.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff main...HEAD touches exactly benchmarks/fixture_positional_stiffness.py, tests/test_fixture_positional_stiffness_render.py, docs/plans/figure-and-solver-audit.html, docs/evidence/archive/figure-and-solver-audit-landed.html, and files under docs/figures/cut-cell-current-attribution/positional-stiffness/ — all within the declared fence, with two commits. The worker correctly did not resolve its own driving followups or set a plan-level terminal status ('Node not closed by this worker'). Docked slightly, not for path discipline, for the manifest's own disclosure of running well past the 40-minute time fence; it was disclosed rather than hidden and no further analysis was added after the fence per the manifest, which is the right response once over budget, but the overrun itself is a discipline lapse worth naming.
